extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, agents, and Patent Office staff (United Kingdom, Patents Rules 1890)
extracted.subtask_description: procedural and substantive rules for filing, processing, opposing, amending, drawing standards, fees, notice, and related conduct under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Acts as implemented by the Patents Rules 1890 (Board of Trade).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short title
rubrics_metrics.description: These Rules may be cited as the Patents Rules, 1890.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: These Rules shall come into operation from and immediately after the 31st day of March 1890.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of terms
rubrics_metrics.description: In the construction of these Rules, any words herein used defined by the said Act shall have the meanings thereby assigned to them respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees to be paid under the Acts shall be those specified in the list of fees in the First Schedule to these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory forms and form substitutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms A, B, and C in the First Schedule to the Act shall be altered by substitution of Forms A, Al, A2, B, and C in the Second Schedule to these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form required for application and specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent containing the declaration mentioned in the Acts shall be made in Form A or Form Al or Form A2; provisional specification in Form B; complete specification in Form C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remaining forms in the Second Schedule may be used in proceedings as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office hours
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office shall be open to the public every weekday between the hours of [office hours stated] except on enumerated holidays (Christmas Day, Good Friday, Her Majesty's birthday, days of public fast/thanksgiving or Bank of England holidays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and agent authorisation
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent must be signed by the applicant; other communications and attendances may be made by or through an agent duly authorised to the satisfaction of the Comptroller, and, if he so requires, resident in the United Kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address for service
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be accompanied by a statement of an address to which all notices, requisitions, and communications may be made; that statement binds the applicant until a substituted address is furnished. The Comptroller may in any case require that the address be in the United Kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document format and language
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents and copies (except statutory declarations and affidavits) furnished to the Patent Office shall be written or printed in large and legible characters and, unless otherwise directed, in the English language, upon strong wide ruled paper (one side only) of a size of 13 inches by 8 inches, leaving a margin of 2 inches on the left-hand part, and signatures must be large and legible. Duplicate documents to be left if required by the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice before adverse exercise of discretionary power
rubrics_metrics.description: Before exercising any discretionary power given to the Comptroller adversely to the applicant, the Comptroller shall give ten days' notice, or longer if he thinks fit, to the applicant of the time when he may be heard personally or by agent before the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory declarations and affidavits shall be in the form for the time being in use in the High Court of Justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply whether applicant intends to be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: Within five days from the date when such notice would be delivered in the ordinary course of post (or longer time appointed by the Comptroller), the applicant shall notify in writing whether or not he intends to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller may require statement or oral explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not the applicant desires to be heard, the Comptroller may at any time require him to submit a written statement within a notified time, or to attend and make oral explanations with respect to such matters as the Comptroller may require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Comptroller's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision or determination of the Comptroller in the exercise of discretionary powers shall be notified by him to the applicant and any other person affected thereby.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice for exhibiting/publishing/using at exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to exhibit an invention at an industrial or international exhibition, to publish any description during the exhibition, or to use the invention for the purpose of the exhibition shall, after Board of Trade issues certificate that the exhibition is industrial/international, give the Comptroller written notice of intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To identify the invention for possible subsequent patent application, the applicant shall furnish a brief description, accompanied if necessary by drawings and such other information as the Comptroller may require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to amend documents and correct irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document for which no special provision is made may be amended, and any irregularity in procedure which in the opinion of the Comptroller may be obviated without detriment to any person's interests may be corrected, on such terms as the Comptroller thinks fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by post deemed delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application, notice, or other document authorised or required to be left or given at the Patent Office or to the Comptroller may be sent by prepaid letter through the post and if so sent shall be deemed to have been left/made/given at the time the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In proving such service, it shall be sufficient to show the letter was properly addressed and put into the post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths, statutory declarations and affidavits — where to be made
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory declarations and affidavits required by the Acts or Rules shall be made before authorised persons: in the United Kingdom before any Justice of the Peace or any Commissioner or other officer authorised by law to administer an oath; elsewhere in Her Majesty's dominions before any court/judge/justice/officer authorised; and out of Her Majesty's dominions before a British minister, consul, vice-consul, person exercising functions of British consul, notary public, judge, or magistrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of statutory declarations and affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory declarations and affidavits shall be headed with the matter to which they relate, divided into consecutively numbered paragraphs, each paragraph confined as far as possible to one subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and numbering of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications sent through the post shall, as far as practicable, be opened and numbered in the order the letters have been delivered in the ordinary course of post; applications left at the Patent Office otherwise shall be numbered in like manner in order of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple inventions in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person by mistake or otherwise includes more than one invention in an application, he may, after refusal to accept, amend to apply to one invention only and may make separate applications for the others; such subsequent applications shall, if the applicant notifies his desire, bear the date of the first application and be proceeded with as if originally made on that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by legal representative of deceased inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: An application by the legal representative of a deceased person possessed of an invention shall be accompanied by an official copy or extract of the will or letters of administration in proof of title, and supported by further evidence the Comptroller may require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and advertisement of acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: On acceptance of a provisional or complete specification the Comptroller shall give notice to the applicant and shall advertise such acceptance in the official journal of the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection after advertisement of acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication of advertisement of acceptance in the case of a complete specification, the application and specification(s) with drawings may be inspected at the Patent Office upon payment of the prescribed fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for patent communicated from abroad (Form Al)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent for an invention communicated from abroad shall be made in the form Al set forth in the Second Schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Office requires applicants using Form Al must be resident in the United Kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'foreign application'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'foreign application' means an application by any person for protection in a Foreign State or British Possession to which, by order in council, section 103 of the Act has been declared applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of foreign applications in UK filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application in the United Kingdom for an invention in respect of which a foreign application has been made shall contain a declaration that such foreign application has been made and shall specify all Foreign States/British Possessions and the official date(s) thereof; the application must be made within 7 months from the date of the first foreign application and signed by the person(s) by whom such first foreign application was made (or by the legal personal representative if dead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required with UK application corresponding to first foreign application
rubrics_metrics.description: The UK application (Form Al) must be accompanied by a copy or copies of the specification and drawings or documents corresponding thereto filed or deposited with the Patent Office of the foreign state or British Possession in respect of the first foreign application, duly certified by the official chief/head of that Patent Office or otherwise verified to the satisfaction of the Comptroller; and a statutory declaration as to identity of the invention, with translation annexed and verified if documents are in a foreign language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller to record applications and dates
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of the application with prescribed payment and accompanying documents and any other proof required, the Comptroller shall make an entry of the applications and of the official dates of such applications respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further proceedings follow ordinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All further proceedings in connection with such application shall be taken within the times and in the manner prescribed by the Acts or Rules for ordinary applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent dated from first foreign application
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent shall be entered in the register dated as of the date on which the first foreign application was made, and payment of renewal fees and expiration shall be reckoned from the date of the first foreign application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings optional but recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisional or complete specification need not be accompanied by drawings if the specification sufficiently describes the invention; but if drawings are furnished they should accompany the specification to which they refer (except as provided by Rule 88).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen drawing layout and paper size
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must follow specimen layout: border line half an inch from edge; size of paper preferably 13 inches by 8 inches or 13 by 16 inches including margin (smaller preferable). If more figures than fit use multiple smaller sheets; exceptionally large drawings continued on subsequent sheets; no limit to number of sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: No letterpress-type sketches in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: No drawing or sketch such as requires a special engraving for letterpress should appear in the specification itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery condition of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be delivered either flat or on rollers so as to be free from folds, breaks, or creases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and materials for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on pure white, hot-pressed, rolled, or calendered drawing paper of smooth surface and good quality and where possible without colour or Indian-ink washes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings are copied at the Patent Office for publication by photo-lithography; this rule must be strictly observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet size, margin, and multiple-sheet handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be on sheets of either 13 by 8 inches or 13 by 16 inches including a half-inch margin; use smaller sheets (13x8) in preference; use two or more sheets rather than the larger size if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution and reproduction quality of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure satisfactory reproduction drawings must be executed with absolutely black Indian ink; maintain the same strength and colour of fine and shade lines throughout; section and shading lines must not be closely drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference figures and letters must be bold, distinct, not less than 1/8 of an inch in height; same letters used in different views of same parts; in complicated drawings reference letters shown outside figure and connected by a fine line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale adopted should be large enough to show clearly wherein the invention consists; denote scale by a drawn scale (not words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labelling of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must bear the name of the applicant (and where applicable the number and year of application) in the left-hand top corner; the number of sheets and the number of each sheet in the right-hand top corner; and the signature of the applicant or agent in the right-hand bottom corner.

rubrics_metrics.name: No written description on drawing face
rubrics_metrics.description: No written description of the [invention] should appear on the [face of the drawing].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule text truncated in source; intent is to forbid written description on drawing sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wood engravings and non-conforming illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Wood engravings, or representations of the invention other than the prescribed drawings, will not be received unless of such a character as to be suitable for reproduction by photo-lithography.

rubrics_metrics.name: True-copy facsimile of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A facsimile of the original drawings, but without colour or Indian-ink washes and prepared strictly in accordance with the drawing regulations, must accompany the originals and be marked 'true copy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt provisional drawings for complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant desires to adopt the drawings lodged with his provisional specification as the drawings for his complete specification, he should refer to them as those 'left with the provisional specification.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of notice of opposition to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of opposition to the grant of a patent shall be in Form D and shall state the ground(s) on which the opponent intends to oppose, be signed, state an address for service in the United Kingdom, and be accompanied by an unstamped copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On receipt the copy shall be transmitted by the Comptroller to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition ground of prior patent must specify prior application number/date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where one ground of opposition is that the invention has been patented in this country on an application of prior date, the number and date of such prior application shall be specified in the notice of opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for leaving evidence in support of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days after the expiration of two months from the date of the advertisement of acceptance of a complete specification, the opponent may leave at the Patent Office statutory declarations in support of his opposition and shall deliver to the applicant a list thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's and opponent's answer and reply declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days from delivery of such list the applicant may leave statutory declarations in answer, delivering a list to the opponent; within 14 days from such delivery the opponent may leave statutory declarations in reply, confined strictly to matters in reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of the declarations may be obtained from the Patent Office or from the opposite party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on further evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: No further evidence shall be left on either side except by closing of leave of the Comptroller upon written consent of the parties or by special leave of the Comptroller on written application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of application for leave to adduce further evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party making such application shall give notice thereof to the opposite party, who shall be entitled to oppose the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing appointment and right to be heard (Form E)
rubrics_metrics.description: On completion of evidence the Comptroller shall appoint a time for hearing and give parties at least ten days' notice; if a party desires to be heard he must forthwith send the Comptroller an application on Form E. The Comptroller may refuse to hear a party who has not sent such application; if neither party applies to be heard, the Comptroller shall decide and notify his decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: No opposition on grounds not stated in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: At the hearing no opposition shall be allowed in respect of any ground not stated in the notice of opposition; and where a ground is prior patent, opposition shall not be allowed unless the prior application's number and date were specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition alleging applicant obtained invention from opponent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ground is that the applicant obtained the invention from the opponent or a person of whom the opponent is legal representative, unless evidence supporting the allegation be left within the prescribed time the opposition shall be deemed abandoned and a patent shall be sealed forthwith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Comptroller's decision after hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the Comptroller after hearing any party who applies to be heard shall be notified by him to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of payment/renewal and renewal fees due at 4th/8th year
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee intends at the expiration of the fourth or eighth year from the date of his patent to keep it in force he shall before the expiration pay the prescribed fee of 50l. or 100l. as the case may be; on compliance the Comptroller shall issue a certificate that payment has been duly made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents granted before commencement the rule is to be read as if 'seventh year' were substituted where appropriate; the patentee may instead pay annual fees in lieu, before expiration of fourth and each succeeding year until inclusive of the thirteenth year, using Form J.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for enlargement of time for payment
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for an enlargement of time for a prescribed payment shall state in detail the circumstances in which, by accident, mistake, or inadvertence, the patentee failed to make such payment; the Comptroller may require substantiating proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for enlargement of time for leaving/accepting complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for enlargement of time for leaving or accepting a complete specification shall state in detail the circumstances and grounds for the extension, and the Comptroller may require substantiating proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: General power to enlarge time
rubrics_metrics.description: The time prescribed by these Rules for doing any act or taking any proceeding may be enlarged by the Comptroller if he thinks fit, upon such notice to other parties and upon such terms as he may direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for leave to amend specification — form and advertisement
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for leave to amend a specification must be signed by the applicant or patentee and accompanied by a duly certified printed copy of the original specification and drawings showing in red ink the proposed amendment, and shall be advertised by publication of the request and nature of the proposed amendment in the official journal and in such other manner as the Comptroller may direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of opposition to amendment — form and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of opposition to an amendment shall state the ground(s) of opposition, be signed, state an address for service in the United Kingdom, and be accompanied by an unstamped copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of such notice shall be transmitted by the Comptroller to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for evidence in amendment opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days after expiration of one month from the first advertisement of the application for leave to amend the opponent may leave statutory declarations in support of his opposition and deliver a list thereof to the applicant; thereafter the provisions applicable to oppositions (Rules 38–44) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations following leave to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Where leave to amend is given the applicant shall, if the Comptroller so requires and within a time limited by him, leave at the Patent Office a new specification and drawings as amended prepared in accordance with Rules 10, 30, and 31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment ordered by Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for leave to amend is made by or in pursuance of an order of the Court or a judge, an official verified copy of the order shall be left with the request at the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement of every amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every amendment of a specification shall be forthwith advertised by the Comptroller in the official journal of the Patent Office and in such other manner as the Comptroller may direct.
